name: Al Salam Bank
founded: 2006 (incorporated in Bahrain and registered with MOIC under CR 59308 on 19 January 2006, per note 1 of the 31 Mar 2026 interim statements)
regulators: Bahrain Bourse and Dubai Financial Market (listed issuer)
DFSA (ASB Capital Limited, DIFC asset manager; Category 3A per launch press)
exchange: Bahrain Bourse; Dubai Financial Market (dual listing)
ownership_summary: Listed on Bahrain Bourse (SALAM) and Dubai Financial Market (SALAM_BAH). The Bourse major-shareholder list names Bank Muscat (S.A.O.G) 14.74%, Muscat Overseas Company LLC 8.43% and Sayacorp B.S.C. (Closed) 6.28%; the remaining ~70.5% is not itemised there. The list is undated (issuer-provided; PDF created 6 Nov 2025). Whether Muscat Overseas Company is linked to Bank Muscat is not stated in the sources opened.
government_link: Not established: the Bourse list names three holders above 5% (S2) and none is identified in the sources opened as a government body; the full shareholder register and the owners of Sayacorp and Muscat Overseas Company were not checked.
group_structure: Al Salam Bank B.S.C. is the parent of a diversified group (note 1, 31 Mar 2026 interim statements, S3): Al Salam Bank - Seychelles Ltd (70.0%, banking), Al Salam Bank Algeria S.P.A. (68.0%, banking), Solidarity Group Holding B.S.C. (c) (55.9%, takaful holding; main subsidiary Solidarity Investment Company B.S.C., a takaful company listed on Bahrain Bourse), ASB Capital Limited (100%, UAE/DIFC asset management) and ASB Finance B.S.C. (c) (100%, formerly Kuwait Finance House (Bahrain) B.S.C. (c), acquired in May 2024). Associates: Gulf African Bank (Kenya, 20.9%) and an economic interest in a 26.2% stake in BBK held via FINCORP W.L.L. (a Shariah financing arrangement, not legal ownership). The figures in this file are group consolidated, so they already include all subsidiaries; none is profiled separately. CAUTION: the entity named 'Kuwait Finance House (Bahrain)' in bh-kfhbahrain is the former Ahli United Bank (renamed Jul 2025), a different bank from the old KFH Bahrain that Al Salam acquired and now holds as ASB Finance.

subsidiaries.name: ASB Capital Limited
subsidiaries.activity: Asset management and investment banking (DIFC-based, DFSA-licensed); launched Nov 2024

subsidiaries.name: Solidarity Group Holding B.S.C. (c)
subsidiaries.activity: Holding company for takaful/insurance business (Solidarity Investment Company B.S.C.)

subsidiaries.name: ASB Finance B.S.C. (c) (formerly Kuwait Finance House (Bahrain) B.S.C. (c))
subsidiaries.activity: Banking services in Bahrain; acquisition completed 15 May 2024

footprint: Bahrain (20 branches), Algeria (26 branches) and Seychelles (1 branch) at 31 Mar 2026 (note 1 of S3), plus ASB Capital in the DIFC (Dubai). Associate in Kenya (Gulf African Bank, 20.9%). Staff numbers not obtained.
customer_segments: Retail, Al Ruwad (affluent/premium tier, no threshold published), Private Banking, corporate, plus institutional and HNW clients of ASB Capital (public markets, private markets, investment banking, placement) and takaful customers through Solidarity.
business_lines: Retail banking (including Al Ruwad and the Al Salam Bank app), corporate banking, private banking, treasury, real estate and investments (incl. an off-balance-sheet investment-management book of BD 796.1m at 31 Mar 2026), asset management and investment banking through ASB Capital (DIFC), takaful through Solidarity Group, and international banking subsidiaries in Algeria and Seychelles. Sharia-compliant throughout (quasi-equity model: customers' current accounts plus wakala and mudaraba accounts).

capabilities.wealth_summary: Al Salam Bank runs its wealth offer through three channels: Al Ruwad (premium retail tier) and Private Banking inside the bank, the Al Salam Invest in-app platform (global equities, ETFs, sukuk and mutual funds, launched around June 2022 for Private Banking and Al Ruwad clients), and ASB Capital, a 100%-owned DIFC asset manager launched in Nov 2024. ASB Capital states AUM of USD 5.8bn (Nov 2025) and USD 10.2bn (Oct 2026) and has launched a State Street Shariah global equity fund (Apr 2025), MENA equity, technology and sukuk funds, the XASB Sukuk ETF on the London Stock Exchange with Xtrackers by DWS (4 Nov 2025; sold in-app from USD 30 per the bank) and, with StepStone, a Shariah private-credit fund (5 Oct 2026). The group's own statements also show BD 796.1m of off-balance-sheet AUM at 31 Mar 2026. No wealth client-asset, user or customer numbers are published in the sources opened, and Al Ruwad and Private Banking eligibility thresholds were not found.

segments.name: Al Ruwad Banking
segments.eligibility: Not published. Benefits listed: dedicated relationship manager, express banking business centres, priority queuing, preferential wakala rates, access to 'exclusive investment opportunities' (search result of the bank's page).

segments.name: Private Banking
segments.eligibility: Not published; Al Salam Invest was launched for Private Banking and Al Ruwad clients.

segments.name: ASB Capital clients
segments.eligibility: Launch coverage says HNWIs, family offices, corporations and institutions across MEA; no minimums found.

private_banking.detail: Private Banking division with a named head on the Bourse key-persons list (Ali Qassim) plus a COO, Private Banking; the bank's website lists it as a business line but thresholds and proposition details were not accessible. Al Salam Invest was launched for Private Banking and Al Ruwad clients in 2022.

asset_management.detail: ASB Capital Limited (100%, DIFC, DFSA Category 3A; launched Nov 2024): four verticals - public markets, private markets, investment banking and placement. Stated AUM USD 4.5bn at launch, USD 5.8bn (Nov 2025), USD 10.2bn (Oct 2026). Funds named in coverage: Shariah global equity (State Street Global Advisors team), MENA equity, technology, sukuk, XASB Sukuk ETF, ASB StepStone Private Financing Fund. Separately, the bank reports BD 796.1m off-balance-sheet AUM (31 Mar 2026).

brokerage.detail: Al Salam Invest, integrated in the Al Salam Bank mobile app, lets Private Banking and Al Ruwad clients trade global equities, ETFs, sukuk and mutual funds in real time (June 2022). Execution partner or broker not named in the sources opened; local Bahrain Bourse brokerage not checked.

digital_investing.detail: Al Salam Invest inside the Al Salam Bank app (app launched 2020 per trade press seen in search results; investing module reported 3 Jun 2022). The bank says the XASB Sukuk ETF can be bought through the app via Al Salam Invest from USD 30 (Nov 2025, search-result summary). App features also include digital onboarding, savings goals, the Danat savings scheme and a Wakala investment account (Feb 2023 article).

advisory.detail: Wealth Management and Private Banking heads are listed; ASB Capital describes 'investment advisory' within integrated solutions (S12). No advisory service description, fee model or suitability process found; website blocked.

discretionary.detail: The group reports BD 796.1m of off-balance-sheet AUM in fixed income, equity and funds, real estate and other portfolios with 'bank's fees as an agent' (S3), which indicates managed portfolios; discretionary mandates are not described and no product page was accessible.

model_portfolios_robo.detail: No model portfolios or robo-advice found in press, statements or the bank's pages seen in search results.

funds_platform.detail: Mutual funds are among the instruments offered on Al Salam Invest (S11). Third-party fund-shelf or platform provider not named. Group funds are sub-advised or partnered: State Street Global Advisors' Active Fundamental Equity team on the Shariah global equity fund, StepStone on the private-credit fund, DWS Xtrackers on the XASB ETF.

structured_products.detail: No structured-product offer found in the sources opened.

private_markets.detail: ASB Capital has a private markets vertical (private equity, venture capital, real estate, private credit per launch coverage); first named product is the ASB StepStone Private Financing Fund, open-ended and perpetual, senior secured US middle-market financing, Shariah-compliant (5 Oct 2026). The bank's off-balance-sheet AUM includes a BD 132.9m real estate portfolio.

islamic_wealth.detail: The whole group is Shariah-compliant: Al Salam Invest is described as Shari'a-compliant; XASB Sukuk ETF tracks the Bloomberg Global Sukuk Index under the ASB Capital Shariah Board; State Street Shariah global equity fund; Shariah private-credit fund.

partners.what: Active Fundamental Equity team manages the ASB Capital Shariah-compliant global equity fund (DIFC-domiciled, DFSA-regulated)
XASB Sukuk ETF listed on the London Stock Exchange (4 Nov 2025); tracks the Bloomberg Global Sukuk Index; first Islamic instrument for Xtrackers per the bank
ASB StepStone Private Financing Fund, a Shariah-compliant open-ended private-credit fund
Equity-accounted associate; Rafik Nayed is its Chairman per Entrepreneur ME

initiatives.what: Al Salam Invest launched inside the Al Salam Bank app for Private Banking and Al Ruwad clients (article dated 3 Jun 2022).

Acquisition of Ithmaar Holding's retail (consumer) banking business, part of a USD 2.2bn asset package that also included 55.91% of Solidarity Group and an interest tied to a 26.19% BBK stake; CBB final approval Jun 2022 and completion reported as Jul 2022 (press, search results only).
Completed acquisition of Kuwait Finance House (Bahrain) B.S.C. (c) (asset base above BD 1.49bn per the bank); now carried as ASB Finance B.S.C. (c).
ASB Capital launched in the DIFC as a DFSA Category 3A asset manager with stated AUM of USD 4.5bn.
ASB Capital and State Street Global Advisors announced a Shariah-compliant global equity fund.
XASB Sukuk ETF (ASB Capital with Xtrackers by DWS) listed on the London Stock Exchange; bank says it is buyable in-app via Al Salam Invest from USD 30.
FY2025 results: record attributable profit BD 76.8m (+30.2%); CEO cites banking, asset management (ASB Capital) and takaful (Solidarity Group) as revenue drivers and a group 'digital in execution'.
H1 2026 results: record semi-annual attributable profit USD 122.8m (+23.8%); total assets USD 22.82bn.
ASB Capital and StepStone launch the ASB StepStone Private Financing Fund (Shariah-compliant private credit); ASB Capital AUM quoted at USD 10.2bn.

opportunities: ASB Capital is building a Shariah product range through partners (State Street Global Advisors, Xtrackers by DWS, StepStone) and states AUM of USD 5.8bn (Nov 2025) and USD 10.2bn (Oct 2026), so it sources third-party and sub-advised products (S12, S13, S16).

Al Salam Invest sells global equities, ETFs, sukuk and mutual funds in the app but was reported only for Private Banking and Al Ruwad clients (S11); the XASB ETF is advertised in-app from USD 30 (S14, search-result summary), a low-ticket channel.
Group CEO frames the group as 'digital in execution' and wants to broaden revenue drivers across banking, ASB Capital and takaful (S5).
Stated plan for ASB Capital's private markets platform to widen with partners ('significant milestone' for its private markets platform, S13) points to appetite for alternatives product sources.
barriers: Islamic-only group: any product shelf must be Shariah-screened and fit the ASB Capital Shariah Board.
Wealth is split across the bank, an in-app platform and an in-house DIFC asset manager (ASB Capital), which already has named product partners (S12, S16).

Al Salam Bank is integrating KFH Bahrain (acquired May 2024, now ASB Finance) and has an economic interest in the BBK stake while BBK/NBB merger talks run, which may absorb management attention (S3, S18).
Wealth and Al Ruwad/Private Banking eligibility, client counts and the Al Salam Invest technology vendor are not published in the sources opened.
incumbent_vendors: State Street Global Advisors - sub-advisor of the ASB Capital Shariah global equity fund (S16)
Xtrackers by DWS - XASB Sukuk ETF provider (S14)
Al Salam Invest platform/execution provider: not named in any source opened

discrepancies.field: Customer deposits: release headline vs statement lines
discrepancies.detail: Releases give customer deposits of BD 5.64bn (31 Mar 2026) and BD 5.48bn (31 Dec 2025). The statements show customers' current accounts plus wakala and mudaraba from customers (quasi-equity) of BD 5,567.7m and BD 5,317.5m, i.e. BD 72m and BD 162m lower.
discrepancies.resolution: Headline recorded as the issuer's own 'customer deposits' with status Requires verification; statement components stated in notes. The bridge was not obtainable (FY2025 statements and annual report blocked).

discrepancies.detail: FY2025 release prints BD 4.10bn (USD 10.79bn), the Q1 2026 statements show 'Financing contracts' of BD 4,066.8m, and the Q1 release says BD 4.08bn is +0.4% on year end.
discrepancies.resolution: Statement figure used; BD 4.10bn in S5 treated as a rounding slip (USD figure matches BD 4.07bn).

discrepancies.detail: The brief said Al Salam 'absorbed Ithmaar Bank's banking business in 2022'. Press says it bought Ithmaar Holding's consumer (retail) banking business, not the whole of Ithmaar Bank, which stays a licensed bank under Ithmaar Holding; the 31 Mar 2026 note 7 describes it as 'the retail business of Ithmaar Holding'. Press gives completion as Jul 2022.
discrepancies.resolution: Recorded as the acquisition of Ithmaar's retail business (2022). Ithmaar Bank's post-deal status rests on a search summary only.

discrepancies.detail: USD 4.5bn (Nov 2024 launch), USD 5.8bn (Nov 2025) and USD 10.2bn (Oct 2026) are company-stated and undated; the group's off-balance-sheet AUM is BD 796.1m (about USD 2.1bn at the peg) at 31 Mar 2026.
discrepancies.resolution: All recorded with their scopes; no reconciliation between ASB Capital AUM and the off-balance-sheet statement was found.

discrepancies.field: Deputy CEO and retail head on key-persons list
discrepancies.detail: The Bourse list shows 'Anwar Murad - Deputy CEO' and both 'Mohammed Hasan Janahi - EVP Retail Banking' and 'Mohammed Buhijji - Head of Retail'; a LinkedIn search surfaced 'Anwar Khalifa - Deputy CEO'.
discrepancies.resolution: Role status left as Requires verification; official leadership page needed.

discrepancies.detail: Al Salam acquired the old Kuwait Finance House (Bahrain) B.S.C. (c) (May 2024), now ASB Finance. The existing bh-kfhbahrain file covers a different entity: the former Ahli United Bank, renamed Kuwait Finance House B.S.C. (c) in Jul 2025.
discrepancies.resolution: No change made to the other file; flagged for central review.
